title: Graphs of Linear Equations
seo_title: Linear Graphs – JSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Plot points on the Cartesian plane; draw graphs of linear equations from a table of values; find the gradient and intercept. (summary of the NERDC JSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 maths worksheets on graphs: coordinates in four quadrants, tables of values, straight-line graphs, gradient and y-intercept. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: m is the gradient, c is the y-intercept.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A point (x, y): go across x, then up y.
  • Make a table of values, plot the points and join them with a straight line.
  • In y = mx + c, m is the gradient (steepness) and c is where the line crosses the y-axis.

Examples

Example

y = 2x − 1 when x = 3

2 × 3 − 1

Answer: y = 5, so (3, 5) is on the line

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Plotting (y, x)x first, then y.
Reading the gradient upside downGradient = rise ÷ run.
Joining points with curvesLinear graphs are straight lines.

sets.title: Is the point on the line?

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 2x − 4?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 2 × 0 − 4 = −4, which matches. So (0, −4).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 4x + 2?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 4 × 1 + 2 = 6, which matches. So (1, 6).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 2x + 2?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 2 × 1 + 2 = 4, which matches. So (1, 4).

items.q: Which point lies on the line y = 2x + 1?
items.e: Substitute the x-coordinate: 2 × 2 + 1 = 5, which matches. So (2, 5).

items.q: Where does the line y = 2x + 4 cross the y-axis?
items.e: The line crosses the y-axis when x = 0, at y = c: (0, 4).

items.q: What is the gradient of the line y = 4x + 4?
items.e: In y = mx + c, the gradient is the number in front of x: 4.

items.q: What is the gradient of the line y = 5 − 2x?
items.e: Write it as y = −2x + 5: the gradient is −2.

items.e: In y = mx + c, the gradient is the number in front of x: 12.

items.q: What is the gradient of the line 3y = −12x − 3?
items.e: Divide by 3 first: y = −4x − 1. The gradient is −4.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (4, −2) and (−1, 3).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (3 − (−2)) ÷ (−1 − 4) = 5 ÷ −5 = −1.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (0, −5) and (2, −7).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (−7 − (−5)) ÷ (2 − 0) = −2 ÷ 2 = −1.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (0, 3) and (−5, −2).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (−2 − 3) ÷ (−5 − 0) = −5 ÷ −5 = 1.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (2, −2) and (5, 1).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (1 − (−2)) ÷ (5 − 2) = 3 ÷ 3 = 1.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (3, 3) and (5, 6).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (6 − 3) ÷ (5 − 3) = 3 ÷ 2 = 32.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (9, 0) and (4, 5).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (5 − 0) ÷ (4 − 9) = 5 ÷ −5 = −1.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (1, 4) and (3, 10).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (10 − 4) ÷ (3 − 1) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (6, 3) and (3, 0).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (0 − 3) ÷ (3 − 6) = −3 ÷ −3 = 1.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (0, 5) and (1, 3).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (3 − 5) ÷ (1 − 0) = −2 ÷ 1 = −2.

items.q: Find the gradient of the line through (2, 3) and (4, −3).
items.e: Gradient = change in y ÷ change in x = (−3 − 3) ÷ (4 − 2) = −6 ÷ 2 = −3.

items.q: What is the equation of the line?
items.e: It crosses the y-axis at 0, so c = 0. For every 1 across it goes down 12, so m = −12. y = −12x.
